# Changelog Generation

Generate a changelog entry for a new release by analyzing merged PRs since the last tag.

## Parameters

The user provides:
- **Version number** -- e.g., `0.5.3`
- **Additional PRs** -- optionally, PRs not yet merged that should be included

## Step 1: Gather Data

1. Find the previous release tag: `git tag --sort=-version:refname | head -1`
2. List all merge commits since that tag: `git log <tag>..HEAD --merges --format='%s' | grep -v "Merge branch"`
3. Get PR details with: `gh pr list --state merged --base main --search "merged:><tag-date>" --json number,title,author --limit 50`
4. List contributors: `git log <tag>..HEAD --format='%an' --no-merges | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`

## Step 2: Identify External Contributors

To determine if a contributor is external, check for an `@entire.io` email:

```bash
git log --all --format='%an <%ae>' --author="<name>" | sort -u
```

If they have an `@entire.io` email anywhere in git history, they are **internal**. Only list external contributors in the Thanks section.

Also check the memory file at `memory/project_team_members.md` for known internal/external mappings.

## Step 3: Write the Entry

Insert the new version section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, after the header and before the previous version.

### Format

Follow the existing style in CHANGELOG.md exactly:

```markdown
## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD

### Added

- Feature description with context ([#123](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/123))

### Changed

- Change description ([#456](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/456))

### Fixed

- Bug fix description ([#789](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/789))

### Housekeeping

- Maintenance item ([#101](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/101))

### Thanks

Thanks to @contributor for description of contribution!
```

### Style Rules

- **Sections**: Added, Changed, Fixed, Housekeeping, Thanks. Omit empty sections.
- **Each bullet**: starts with a dash, concise description, PR link(s) at the end
- **Group related PRs** into a single bullet when they're part of the same feature/fix
- **Work-in-progress features**: call out explicitly, e.g., "Feature X (work in progress): ..."
- **Known limitations**: note inline, e.g., "Note: subagent tracking is not yet supported due to..."
- **Thanks section**: only external contributors. Name what they contributed specifically.
- **Dependency bumps**: group into a single Housekeeping bullet unless a bump fixes a notable bug
- **PR links**: always use full URL format `[#N](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/N)`
- **No trailing period** on bullet items
- **Date**: use the current date in YYYY-MM-DD format

### Categorization Guide

- **Added**: new features, new commands, new agent integrations, new CI workflows
- **Changed**: behavior changes, API changes, UX changes, migrations
- **Fixed**: bug fixes, E2E fixes, agent-specific fixes
- **Housekeeping**: dependency bumps, docs, refactors, CI improvements, test improvements

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [0.10.2] - 2026-08-19

### Added

- Better subagent handling for Codex and Cursor (subagent tracking remains work in progress): Entire now consumes Codex's `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` hooks, and an agent can declare its own subagent transcript path instead of having the Claude Code layout guessed for it — which also fixes Cursor, which had parsed that path all along and dropped it. This is the in-session half only. Committed checkpoints still carry no per-subagent data for any agent, Codex does not aggregate subagent token usage, and only thread-spawned Codex subagents fire the hooks ([#1958](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1958))
- `entire repo create --object-format` selects `sha1` or `sha256`, validated client-side so a typo fails fast instead of coming back as an opaque 422 ([#2043](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2043))

### Changed

- The `entire search` TUI drops its Checkpoints tab and defaults to Sessions. Search now folds checkpoint hits into their owning sessions server-side, so the old default tab always showed zero results; a checkpoint stays reachable by ID via `entire checkpoint explain` ([#2022](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2022))

### Security

- `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command` is honored only from a `.entire/settings.local.json` verified to be untracked. It becomes `argv[0]` of an exec on every push, and was read from the version-controlled `.entire/settings.json` with no validation — so a pull request could pair the setting with a payload committed alongside it and run code on every developer who pushes, including non-interactively in CI. A tracked `settings.local.json` is now ignored wholesale, since `.gitignore` does not apply to an already-tracked path. Rejection downgrades to resolving `opf` on `$PATH` rather than erroring, and the rewrite fails closed if that is missing ([#2056](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2056))

### Fixed

- Repo-scoped data could be read from the wrong region. Cell resolution scanned mirrors and silently fell back to the caller's home cell whenever a repo was mirrored in more than one region, so `entire trail list --repo <multi-region repo>` printed "No open trails found" instead of the repo's real trails. Resolution now goes through the repo's processing placement, and every failure is a returned error instead of a silent fallback. `entire agent-help`'s trails probe and `entire enable`'s post-success report had the same bug against the BFF, which does not proxy trails for CLI bearers ([#2046](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2046), [#2047](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2047))
- A repo that is not onboarded — or not visible to your login — is now named in one honest line across `entire trail`, `entire experts`, and `entire checkpoint explain --repo`, instead of an anonymous "This repository" on one surface and a raw internal resolution chain on the others. Single-repo cell resolution also tolerates the same catalog gaps the multi-repo fan-out already survived, and `entire enable`'s trails probe gets its own deadline so a slow enable report can no longer starve it ([#2054](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2054))
- `entire trail update --body` never worked: the description was sent as a field on the metadata `PATCH`, a route that does not serve body writes, and the rejection arrived as a bare `Service Unavailable`. Descriptions now go to the dedicated body route, and `--body=` clears one ([#2055](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2055))
- Cloud-mode `entire dispatch` sends `entire-cli/<version>` as its User-Agent instead of Go's default, so its traffic is no longer invisible to server-side CLI version gating ([#2049](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2049))

### Housekeeping

- `go-runewidth` moves to 0.0.28 and the version pin from 0.10.1 is dropped — upstream builds its width table lazily now, so startup stays at ~18ms without pinning ([#2040](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2040))
- Trail wire handling consumes entire-api's camelCase contract directly, dropping the remaining snake_case JSON and SSE normalization along with obsolete list-response compatibility fields ([#2037](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2037))
- The Linux CI test jobs no longer `apt-get install gnome-keyring`: the token store has resolved to a temp file backend under test for some time, and the step's only remaining effect was to make three PR-blocking jobs depend on an Ubuntu mirror that intermittently hung them for the full 6-hour default timeout. Those jobs now also carry a 30-minute timeout ([#2072](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2072))

## [0.10.1] - 2026-08-18

### Added

- `entire login` keeps the authorization URL visible and clickable, starts waiting for the callback immediately, and offers Enter to open the browser or `c` to copy — so a login can be finished in a different browser or profile without a terminal keypress ([#1961](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1961))
- Checkpoints now follow the remote you actually push to: when a push agrees with your branch's declared push destination, that observed remote is recorded as the checkpoint sync remote, announced on stderr, and the same push carries the checkpoints. `entire status` shows it as "follows your branch's push destination" ([#1991](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1991), [#2036](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2036))
- On the git-refs backend, a fresh clone discovers checkpoints without a dedicated `checkpoint_remote` — `checkpoint list` and the branch view ls-remote the read candidates and merge the listings ([#1956](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1956))
- `entire trail show --json` prints one trail object in the same shape as an entry of `trail list --json` ([#1970](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1970))

### Changed

- `entire login` defaults to `https://auth.entire.io` and follows its regional handoff, exchanging the code at the region that minted it; `--server` stays for special cases ([#1945](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1945))
- Commands no longer pick a login for you. When several logins are saved, the acting identity must be selected explicitly — `entire auth use`, or `--context` / `ENTIRE_CONTEXT` for one-offs. Previously adding a second login could silently change which identity an existing command authenticated as ([#1982](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1982))
- `entire trail` talks to entire-api directly; the legacy backend and `ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND` are retired ([#1949](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1949), [#2021](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2021))
- `local_dev` mode is removed. It existed only to dogfood unreleased changes in this repo, pointing installed hooks at a launcher inside the working tree. Hooks now always name the `entire` binary, the `--local-dev` flags and `scripts/entire-dev` are gone, and the settings key is accepted as a documented no-op so existing settings files still parse ([#1999](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1999))
- Checkpoint reads follow the elected sync remote, with `origin` kept as a read-only legacy tier. Reads previously hardcoded `origin`, so a repo with `checkpoint_push_remote` set — or with no `origin` at all — wrote checkpoints it could never read back ([#1951](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1951))
- A push that does not carry checkpoints now says so on stderr, naming the sync remote and the setting to change, instead of stranding them silently ([#1987](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1987))

### Fixed

- `entire login` on Windows opened a truncated authorization URL and was rejected for a missing `redirect_uri`; the browser now launches via `ShellExecute` instead of `cmd /c start`, which cut the URL at its first `&` ([#1981](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1981))
- Every `entire` invocation is roughly 1.9× faster to start — 33.8ms → 18.0ms — by dropping a 2.2MB lookup table that `go-runewidth` v0.0.26 built in `init()` on every run, including every agent hook fire ([#2026](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2026))
- Codex sessions no longer pile up: Codex's `SessionEnd` hook is now registered, and the dead-owner sweep in `entire status` / `entire doctor` also covers sessions whose agent quit after its last turn (previously only fully-active ones), so an agent killed before its hook runs is still finalized ([#1940](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1940))
- Codex sessions are titled from the genuine prompt instead of Codex's injected runtime preamble (`<environment_context>`, `# AGENTS.md`, `<recommended_plugins>`, `<user_action>`, `<turn_aborted>`) ([#2016](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2016))
- Factory AI Droid Worker sessions are attributed to their parent task now that Droid dispatches Workers in the background ([#2000](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2000))

############ PR #1877
TITLE: fix(attach): fetch on-demand transcripts for untracked sessions
Fixes #1876.

## Problem

`entire session attach <id> --agent opencode` fails with `transcript not found` for OpenCode sessions Entire never tracked — e.g. sessions spawned by an external session host rather than a hooked terminal. `resolveAndValidateTranscript` only calls `PrepareTranscript` when the transcript file *already exists* under `.entire/tmp`, on the assumption that preparation "can't conjure a file that was never started". For OpenCode that assumption is false: its transcript is produced on demand by `opencode export` (`fetchAndCacheExport`), which works for any session in the opencode store, tracked or not. OpenCode also lacks a `SessionBaseDirProvider`, so the project-dir fallback can't help. Net effect: no way to attach the correct session when hooks didn't capture one.

## Fix

- New optional `TranscriptFetcher` agent capability (`agent.go` + `AsTranscriptFetcher`, type-assertion gated like `SidecarImageProvider`): the agent can materialize a session transcript on demand, including for sessions with no hook-cached file.
- `OpenCodeAgent.FetchTranscript` implements it via the existing `fetchAndCacheExport` (which already honors `ENTIRE_TEST_OPENCODE_MOCK_EXPORT`).
- `resolveAndValidateTranscript` consults the capability after the initial stat fails, before the project-dir search fallback. File-based agents are unaffected.

Out of scope (noted in the issue): `session list` enumeration from the opencode store — the attach path was the workflow blocker.

## Testing

- New regression test `TestAttach_OpenCodeFetchesTranscriptForUntrackedSession`: a session with no hook-cached export attaches successfully via the fetch path (mock-export mode), producing session state with a checkpoint id.
- `TestFetchTranscript_ValidatesSessionID` / `TestFetchTranscript_AttemptsExport` for the new method.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/...` and `golangci-lint run` clean.

## Verification (downstream)

The same scenario was exercised end-to-end against a real externally-hosted OpenCode session (`opencode export` succeeds, attach previously failed); with this change the fetch path materializes the transcript and attach proceeds.

############ PR #1977
TITLE: fix(hooks): bound the agent-hook status walk so pathological repos degrade instead of hanging
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1033

## Motivation

Live incident (2026-08-12): a stray `git init` in a user's `$HOME` (no `.gitignore`) meant every agent Stop hook ran a worktree status walk over the entire home directory. The hook hung >120s; Claude Code stopped waiting at its ~60s hook timeout, but the `entire hooks claude-code stop` **process survived** — two zombies were found hours later at ~1.8GB RSS each, one with 25 CPU-minutes, still writing loose objects (200k+ files) into the repo. The failure was completely silent: no session state, no checkpoint, no log line — the session looked tracked. Trail finding `019ff792-3b10-72af-96d1-ddb7a7874064` on the feat/global-invisible trail documents it; this PR is the fix. The hazard exists on main today for any enabled repo with pathological status cost; global enable amplifies it by lazily enrolling uncurated repos.

## Fix shape

go-git's `Worktree.Status()` (the single sanctioned call site in `gitrepo/status.go`) is **not context-cancellable**, so the budget is a goroutine+select wrapper, `gitrepo.StatusWithBudget`:

- **20s wall-clock budget** (`gitrepo.StatusWalkBudget`): far beyond any healthy repo's walk, while leaving the remaining ~40s of the agent's ~60s hook timeout for the rest of the capture path (transcript copy, tree building, state writes) so the hook exits instead of being orphaned. No new user-facing setting.
- **On breach**: the walk goroutine is abandoned (it dies with the one-shot hook process — that is the point; a `recover` guard keeps an orphaned walk from crashing the hook if the caller closes the repo under it), and the returned error wraps the sentinel `gitrepo.ErrStatusBudgetExceeded`. Context cancellation is treated the same way — it arms the latch and carries the sentinel (with `ctx.Err()` still in the chain) — so a walk abandoned by cancellation cannot fail the hook hard or defeat the fail-open guarantee.
- **Actionable Warn** at breach names the repo root, elapsed, budget, and consequence ("capture degraded: untracked/new file detection skipped this turn") so `doctor logs` investigation finds it. Operational metadata only.
- **Zombie prevention**: a process-local latch makes every later `StatusWithBudget` call in the same hook process fail fast — the turn-start hook walks twice (pre-prompt capture + prompt attribution), and re-entering the walk after a breach is exactly what kept the incident processes alive.
- **The C-git half of the zombie**: the first-checkpoint path in the checkpoint store runs `git status --porcelain -z -uall` as a subprocess with no deadline, so after a go-git breach the hook could still get stuck in a child git instead of a goroutine. That subprocess is now bounded by the same `StatusWalkBudget` via `context.WithTimeout` (`exec.CommandContext` kills the child on expiry) and reports the same sentinel; the lifecycle handlers recognize it and warn-and-skip the checkpoint instead of failing the hook.

## Call sites bounded (agent-hook paths)

- `DetectFileChanges` (turn-end, subagent-end, Claude PostTodo) — errors were already Warn-and-continue.
- Pre-prompt / pre-task untracked scans (`CapturePrePromptState` / `CapturePreTaskState`) — these previously **failed the hook** on status error; they now fail open (hooks must never break the agent) and record an `UntrackedScanSkipped` marker in the state file.
- Prompt-attribution walk in `calculatePromptAttributionAtStart` — already fully fail-open; now also fails fast via the latch after a pre-prompt breach.
- First-checkpoint `git status` subprocess in `checkpoint/ephemeral.go` (`collectChangedFiles`), reached via `SaveStep` — bounded as above; `handleLifecycleTurnEnd` treats the sentinel from a save as warn-and-skip (hook exits 0), and its turn-end tail (LastPrompt backfill, phase transition, pre-prompt cleanup) still runs on that degrade path. The matching branch in `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` is defensive symmetry, not a live path: task saves write via `writeTask`, which reads no worktree status today. The go-git walk budget and this C-git budget deliberately stack (~40s worst case of the ~60s hook timeout) rather than sharing the breach latch — C git is much faster and honors ignores, so it often produces a real first checkpoint where the go-git walk breached, and unlike the walk it is reliably killed on expiry.

Left unbounded deliberately: `checkCanRewindWithWarning` (rewind machinery, no CLI surface), review-worktree removal, and `entire session adopt` — a user is actively waiting on those commands, they are not hook paths, and a slow-but-healthy repo (NFS, cold cache) should finish rather than error at the budget. Adopt originally inherited the budget through `DetectFileChanges`; it now uses an explicit unbounded variant (`detectFileChangesUnbounded`) so the budget stays a hook-path property. Git-hook paths (post-commit condensation) never call Status.

## Degradation semantics

On breach, capture proceeds with transcript-derived files. New-file detection is skipped for the turn: the `UntrackedScanSkipped` marker tells turn-end/subagent-end to drop `changes.New`, because without a pre-prompt baseline every untracked file in the worktree would be misattributed to the agent. This matters precisely in the cross-process shape — turn start breaches (marker written), turn end runs in a fresh process whose walk succeeds — and is covered by dedicated tests that fail if either guard is removed. Modified/deleted detection degrades to nil alongside the status error, as before. A breach inside the save itself (the C-git first-checkpoint read) skips that checkpoint with a Warn and still exits 0.

One deliberate widening beyond the budget feature: the pre-prompt/pre-task untracked scans now fail open on **any** error (repo-open failure, corrupted `.git`, …), not just budget breaches. Previously any status error there failed the TurnStart/SubagentStart hook and broke the agent's turn; that fail-hook behavior was the bug — the scan only feeds new-file detection, so the correct degrade is warn + marker + transcript-derived capture. The code comment at `untrackedFilesOrSkip` states this explicitly.

Degradation is visible outside `.entire/logs`: turn end persists `SessionState.CaptureDegradedAt` when any status scan feeding the turn breached (marker, `DetectFileChanges` sentinel, or a breach inside the save), and clears it on the next healthy turn. `entire status` prints a per-session warning ("capture degraded …: status scan over budget; new-file detection skipped") and `entire status --json` carries `capture_degraded` on the session brief, so a repo that breaches every turn no longer reports a healthy session while new-file detection is silently off.

## Tests

- `TestStatusWithBudget_BreachAbandonsWalkPromptly` — breach surfaces the sentinel at the budget (not when the walk ends) and the latch stops a second walk from starting; pins the zombie regression.
- `TestStatusWithBudget_BreachWarnsWithRepoRoot` — the breach Warn carries the `repo_root` attribute (the incident was silent; this pins the observability).
- `TestTurnFlow_StatusBudgetBreachDegradesGracefully` — same-process shape: full turn-start + turn-end with the latch set; both hooks return success and the checkpoint contains the transcript-derived file.
- `TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_ScanSkippedMarkerSkipsNewFileDetection` / `TestHandleLifecycleSubagentEnd_ScanSkippedMarkerSkipsNewFileDetection` — cross-process shape: marker written under a breach, end-hook walk succeeds; the checkpoint must not claim pre-existing untracked files. Verified by mutation: deleting either `changes.New` guard fails the corresponding test.
- `TestCollectChangedFiles_BudgetExceededReturnsSentinel` — the first-checkpoint `git status` subprocess had no deadline and could outlive the agent's hook timeout; on expiry the error must wrap `gitrepo.ErrStatusBudgetExceeded` so the lifecycle warn-and-skip path recognizes it.
- `TestStatusWithBudget_CancellationArmsLatchAndCarriesSentinel` — a walk abandoned by context cancellation must degrade like a timer breach (sentinel carried, latch armed) while `context.Canceled` stays in the error chain.
- `TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_SaveBreachStillBackfillsLastPrompt` — a breach inside the save must still run the turn-end tail: checkpoint skipped, hook exits 0, LastPrompt backfilled, `CaptureDegradedAt` persisted.
- The marker tests above also pin `CaptureDegradedAt` being set on a degraded turn and cleared by the next healthy one.

## Verification

- `mise run fmt` + `mise run lint` — clean (lint rerun after fmt, 0 issues)
- `mise run test` — 8816 tests passed
- `mise run test:integration` — 472 tests passed
- `mise run test:e2e:canary` — all 56 + 4 tests passed

############ PR #2002
TITLE: perf: stop re-redacting whole transcripts on every checkpoint
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1053
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A Stop hook on a 70MB Codex transcript took **~67s**. Profiling `createRedactedBlobFromFile` put redaction at **99.7%** of it (git object writing was 174ms), and the CPU profile put **82%** of that in betterleaks' regex ruleset under Go's NFA engine:

```
regexp.(*machine).add           43%
regexp/syntax.(*Inst).MatchRunePos  22%
regexp.(*machine).step          15%
  └─ betterleaks/detect.(*Detector).Detect   82% cumulative
```

Two independent problems: each pass was single-threaded, and the *whole* transcript was re-redacted on every checkpoint even though `full.jsonl` is append-only — so a session with N checkpoints re-redacted O(N²) bytes. That second part is also why these repos accumulate multi-GB packs.

## Result

Simulated 14-checkpoint session growing to 70MB:

| | final Stop | cumulative |
|---|---|---|
| main | ~66 s | — |
| + sharding | 18.5 s | 1m 40s |
| + prefix reuse | **2.0 s** | **31 s** |

## Commits

**1. `perf(redact)`: shard JSONL line redaction across goroutines**

Every line is redacted in isolation by a stateless redactor, so the line pass splits. Output is byte-identical.

Shards are sized *by bytes*, not one-per-core, for two measured reasons. Per-byte cost climbs with input size (allocation/GC pressure over one large buffer), so small pieces are cheaper per byte **and** run concurrently — 20MB fixture: 43s sequential vs 2.1s across 12 shards, superlinear in shard count and not explainable by parallelism alone. And balancing by bytes rather than line count matters because transcripts mix thousands of short lines with occasional multi-MB tool results, where equal line counts leave one oversized shard as the tail.

Sharding is gated on an explicit argument describing the **redactor**, not on which entry point was called. `String` is pure and opts in; the OPF collector closures accumulate into a shared map/slice and opt out. Hashes what changes the regex layers' output — custom rules (sorted, so map order can't leak) plus PII enablement, categories, and patterns. `configFingerprintVersion` is mixed in and must be bumped when the layers change behaviour, making it part of the pipeline's contract. Documents the two things it cannot cover: OPF (not a pure function of local config) and the betterleaks version (not exposed by the library).

**3. `perf(checkpoint)`: reuse the redacted transcript prefix across checkpoints**

Keeps the redacted prefix and redacts only what was appended. Soundness rests on two properties:

- Redaction is per-line and stateless, so `redact(A+B) == redact(A)+redact(B)` — now pinned by a test in `redact` itself, since this cache is what depends on it
- A stored prefix always ends immediately after a newline, so the redacted prefix does too and plain byte concatenation reproduces the full result with no boundary fixups

Reuse is refused unless the prefix bytes still hash the same **and** the fingerprint matches, so a rewritten or compacted transcript, changed custom rules, or a CLI upgrade all fall back to redacting everything.

Eligibility keys on `paths.TranscriptFileName`, not a `.jsonl` suffix: only `full.jsonl` is appended to — `transcript.jsonl` is regenerated in full each checkpoint and `full.jsonl.001` chunks aren't appended — so neither qualifies by accident. Stated in the code and CLAUDE.md rather than implied: this covers the **shadow-branch metadata write only**. Condensation (`manual_commit_condensation.go`) and the Stop finalize rewrite (`manual_commit_hooks.go`) still redact whole transcripts — they inherit the sharding but not the prefix reuse, so a mid-turn-commit Stop and every user commit still pay a full pass. Extending it there is the obvious follow-up.

Also not covered: single-JSON-value transcripts (OpenCode export) get neither mechanism, having no line structure to split on.

## Testing

Tests assert the properties, not the timings. Sharded output equals sequential across a fixture exercising every layer, plus shard boundaries and edge shapes. Incremental output equals a full redaction across repeated appends, and every fallback — rewritten prefix, stale fingerprint, corrupt entry, missing blob, partial trailing line, wrong filename, nil cache — produces exactly what redacting the whole file would.

Agent review on the trail found two, both fixed in this PR:

- **High — single-JSON-value transcripts must not be spliced.** OpenCode writes a single JSON object to the same `full.jsonl` path other agents write JSONL to, so the filename gate admitted non-line-delimited content. Splicing a fragment of it drops out of the field-aware pass into raw entropy detection over partial JSON. Now gated on `redact.IsLineDelimited`, which checks the invariant directly instead of inferring it from a filename.
- **Low — the cache is now reclaimed by `entire clean`.** Wired in as `CleanupTypeRedactCache`; the directory is removed wholesale since every entry is rebuildable.

## Summary

Reproduced on a repo with `external_agents: true` and an external plugin whose `are-hooks-installed` reports true:

$ entire disable --uninstall --force

  Removed Claude Code hooks
  Removed git hooks (5)
  Removed .entire directory

Entire CLI uninstalled successfully.

$ # subcommands the plugin was asked to run: (empty — it was never executed, not even `info`)

The plugin's hooks stayed on disk, and because `.entire/` (settings included) had just been deleted, what remained was a set of agent hooks calling into an Entire that is no longer installed there.

## Cause
`runUninstall` reaches agents only through the registry, and nothing on that path ever ran external-agent discovery, so an external agent was not in the registry to be uninstalled: absent from the confirmation summary, its `UninstallHooks` never ran, and its hooks survived an uninstall that reported success.

## Fix
`external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways(ctx)` at the top of `runUninstall` — **ungated, deliberately**. The `external_agents` setting that gates discovery lives in `.entire/`, which this very command deletes. After a partial uninstall (plugin hooks left behind, `.entire/` gone) a gated re-run could never see the plugin again, making the uninstall unrepeatable. Ungated discovery keeps every removal step isolated from the others, at the accepted cost of executing `entire-agent-*` binaries on `$PATH` even in repos that never enabled them.

On top of that:

- **One hooks-installed sweep per uninstall.** The confirmation summary and the removal share the same `getAgentHookState` result — for an external agent each probe is a subprocess, and reusing it means the uninstall removes exactly what the user was shown.
- **Uninstall acts on the sweep's answer, for built-ins and plugins alike.** An agent that cleanly reported no hooks is left alone — `uninstall-hooks` is a mutating call, and discovery registers every `entire-agent-*` on `$PATH`, not just the one the user enabled.
- **`AreHooksInstalled` now returns `(bool, error)` across the agent interface.** Every agent had been collapsing "I cannot tell" (unreadable config, malformed JSON, a plugin that crashed or timed out) into "no hooks installed". An agent that could not answer lands in an `unchecked` set: named in the confirmation summary on its own line, warned about with its own error, and **not** asked to mutate state it never claimed to own.
- **`entire agent remove <name>` fails on a broken check** instead of uninstalling blind — that path targets one agent the user named, so they can fix the config and re-run.
- **The recovery command is one a plugin will accept, and one Windows can run.** It carries `cd <repo-root>`, `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`, and `ENTIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` (the protocol promises all three), quotes paths with spaces, and prints a PowerShell shape on Windows. `TestPluginUninstallCommand_PerOS` pins both shapes.
- **Usable without a terminal.** The confirmation prompt now has an `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` guard pointing at `--force` instead of a bubbletea internal error (which also made the test suite hang under a pty).

## Exit-code contract: any failed step fails the command
There is **no `--strict` flag** (it existed mid-branch and was dropped). The uninstall has a single contract: any step that fails — built-in agent hooks, external plugin hooks, git hooks, session states, `.entire/`, shadow branches — exits non-zero and closes with `Uninstall did not complete — see the warnings above.` A run never reports a success it could not verify:

- An external plugin whose `uninstall-hooks` fails is named with both remedies: re-run `entire disable --uninstall` (discovery is ungated, so a re-run reaches the plugin again), and the direct `entire-agent-<name> uninstall-hooks` command, since the plugin binary itself may be what is broken.
- An **unchecked** agent (probe crashed, errored, or printed junk) also fails the run. Its hooks "may still be installed" — an unknown state is not a clean "none". Unchecked externals get the same two remedies; unchecked built-ins are reported with the read/parse reason (removal would read the same broken file, so it is not attempted, and no plugin command applies).
- The `"Entire is not installed in this repository"` early return requires every agent to have been *checked*: any unchecked agent falls through to the removal phase, so a repo whose only leftover is an unprobeable plugin no longer silently claims "not installed" on re-run.
- The only exception is the user's own Ctrl-C: a cancelled context is reported as an interruption ("run again to finish"), not charged to the agent it happened to kill — still non-zero, but no per-agent blame or recovery command.

✗ Uninstall did not complete — see the warnings above.

Slow external subprocesses run under a live progress line (TTY only), so a hanging plugin is attributable instead of a silent stall.

TITLE: fix(hooks): bound the agent-hook status walk so pathological repos degrade instead of hanging
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1033

## Motivation

Live incident (2026-08-12): a stray `git init` in a user's `$HOME` (no `.gitignore`) meant every agent Stop hook ran a worktree status walk over the entire home directory. The hook hung >120s; Claude Code stopped waiting at its ~60s hook timeout, but the `entire hooks claude-code stop` **process survived** — two zombies were found hours later at ~1.8GB RSS each, one with 25 CPU-minutes, still writing loose objects (200k+ files) into the repo. The failure was completely silent: no session state, no checkpoint, no log line — the session looked tracked. Trail finding `019ff792-3b10-72af-96d1-ddb7a7874064` on the feat/global-invisible trail documents it; this PR is the fix. The hazard exists on main today for any enabled repo with pathological status cost; global enable amplifies it by lazily enrolling uncurated repos.

## Fix shape

go-git's `Worktree.Status()` (the single sanctioned call site in `gitrepo/status.go`) is **not context-cancellable**, so the budget is a goroutine+select wrapper, `gitrepo.StatusWithBudget`:

- **20s wall-clock budget** (`gitrepo.StatusWalkBudget`): far beyond any healthy repo's walk, while leaving the remaining ~40s of the agent's ~60s hook timeout for the rest of the capture path (transcript copy, tree building, state writes) so the hook exits instead of being orphaned. No new user-facing setting.
- **On breach**: the walk goroutine is abandoned (it dies with the one-shot hook process — that is the point; a `recover` guard keeps an orphaned walk from crashing the hook if the caller closes the repo under it), and the returned error wraps the sentinel `gitrepo.ErrStatusBudgetExceeded`. Context cancellation is treated the same way — it arms the latch and carries the sentinel (with `ctx.Err()` still in the chain) — so a walk abandoned by cancellation cannot fail the hook hard or defeat the fail-open guarantee.
- **Actionable Warn** at breach names the repo root, elapsed, budget, and consequence ("capture degraded: untracked/new file detection skipped this turn") so `doctor logs` investigation finds it. Operational metadata only.
- **Zombie prevention**: a process-local latch makes every later `StatusWithBudget` call in the same hook process fail fast — the turn-start hook walks twice (pre-prompt capture + prompt attribution), and re-entering the walk after a breach is exactly what kept the incident processes alive.
- **The C-git half of the zombie**: the first-checkpoint path in the checkpoint store runs `git status --porcelain -z -uall` as a subprocess with no deadline, so after a go-git breach the hook could still get stuck in a child git instead of a goroutine. That subprocess is now bounded by the same `StatusWalkBudget` via `context.WithTimeout` (`exec.CommandContext` kills the child on expiry) and reports the same sentinel; the lifecycle handlers recognize it and warn-and-skip the checkpoint instead of failing the hook.

## Call sites bounded (agent-hook paths)

- `DetectFileChanges` (turn-end, subagent-end, Claude PostTodo) — errors were already Warn-and-continue.
- Pre-prompt / pre-task untracked scans (`CapturePrePromptState` / `CapturePreTaskState`) — these previously **failed the hook** on status error; they now fail open (hooks must never break the agent) and record an `UntrackedScanSkipped` marker in the state file.
- Prompt-attribution walk in `calculatePromptAttributionAtStart` — already fully fail-open; now also fails fast via the latch after a pre-prompt breach.
- First-checkpoint `git status` subprocess in `checkpoint/ephemeral.go` (`collectChangedFiles`), reached via `SaveStep` — bounded as above; `handleLifecycleTurnEnd` treats the sentinel from a save as warn-and-skip (hook exits 0), and its turn-end tail (LastPrompt backfill, phase transition, pre-prompt cleanup) still runs on that degrade path. The matching branch in `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` is defensive symmetry, not a live path: task saves write via `writeTask`, which reads no worktree status today. The go-git walk budget and this C-git budget deliberately stack (~40s worst case of the ~60s hook timeout) rather than sharing the breach latch — C git is much faster and honors ignores, so it often produces a real first checkpoint where the go-git walk breached, and unlike the walk it is reliably killed on expiry.

Left unbounded deliberately: `checkCanRewindWithWarning` (rewind machinery, no CLI surface), review-worktree removal, and `entire session adopt` — a user is actively waiting on those commands, they are not hook paths, and a slow-but-healthy repo (NFS, cold cache) should finish rather than error at the budget. Adopt originally inherited the budget through `DetectFileChanges`; it now uses an explicit unbounded variant (`detectFileChangesUnbounded`) so the budget stays a hook-path property. Git-hook paths (post-commit condensation) never call Status.

## Degradation semantics

On breach, capture proceeds with transcript-derived files. New-file detection is skipped for the turn: the `UntrackedScanSkipped` marker tells turn-end/subagent-end to drop `changes.New`, because without a pre-prompt baseline every untracked file in the worktree would be misattributed to the agent. This matters precisely in the cross-process shape — turn start breaches (marker written), turn end runs in a fresh process whose walk succeeds — and is covered by dedicated tests that fail if either guard is removed. Modified/deleted detection degrades to nil alongside the status error, as before. A breach inside the save itself (the C-git first-checkpoint read) skips that checkpoint with a Warn and still exits 0.

One deliberate widening beyond the budget feature: the pre-prompt/pre-task untracked scans now fail open on **any** error (repo-open failure, corrupted `.git`, …), not just budget breaches. Previously any status error there failed the TurnStart/SubagentStart hook and broke the agent's turn; that fail-hook behavior was the bug — the scan only feeds new-file detection, so the correct degrade is warn + marker + transcript-derived capture. The code comment at `untrackedFilesOrSkip` states this explicitly.

Degradation is visible outside `.entire/logs`: turn end persists `SessionState.CaptureDegradedAt` when any status scan feeding the turn breached (marker, `DetectFileChanges` sentinel, or a breach inside the save), and clears it on the next healthy turn. `entire status` prints a per-session warning ("capture degraded …: status scan over budget; new-file detection skipped") and `entire status --json` carries `capture_degraded` on the session brief, so a repo that breaches every turn no longer reports a healthy session while new-file detection is silently off.

## Tests

- `TestStatusWithBudget_BreachAbandonsWalkPromptly` — breach surfaces the sentinel at the budget (not when the walk ends) and the latch stops a second walk from starting; pins the zombie regression.
- `TestStatusWithBudget_BreachWarnsWithRepoRoot` — the breach Warn carries the `repo_root` attribute (the incident was silent; this pins the observability).
- `TestTurnFlow_StatusBudgetBreachDegradesGracefully` — same-process shape: full turn-start + turn-end with the latch set; both hooks return success and the checkpoint contains the transcript-derived file.
- `TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_ScanSkippedMarkerSkipsNewFileDetection` / `TestHandleLifecycleSubagentEnd_ScanSkippedMarkerSkipsNewFileDetection` — cross-process shape: marker written under a breach, end-hook walk succeeds; the checkpoint must not claim pre-existing untracked files. Verified by mutation: deleting either `changes.New` guard fails the corresponding test.
- `TestCollectChangedFiles_BudgetExceededReturnsSentinel` — the first-checkpoint `git status` subprocess had no deadline and could outlive the agent's hook timeout; on expiry the error must wrap `gitrepo.ErrStatusBudgetExceeded` so the lifecycle warn-and-skip path recognizes it.
- `TestStatusWithBudget_CancellationArmsLatchAndCarriesSentinel` — a walk abandoned by context cancellation must degrade like a timer breach (sentinel carried, latch armed) while `context.Canceled` stays in the error chain.
- `TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_SaveBreachStillBackfillsLastPrompt` — a breach inside the save must still run the turn-end tail: checkpoint skipped, hook exits 0, LastPrompt backfilled, `CaptureDegradedAt` persisted.
- The marker tests above also pin `CaptureDegradedAt` being set on a degraded turn and cleared by the next healthy one.

- Redaction is per-line and stateless, so `redact(A+B) == redact(A)+redact(B)` — now pinned by a test in `redact` itself, since this cache is what depends on it
- A stored prefix always ends immediately after a newline, so the redacted prefix does too and plain byte concatenation reproduces the full result with no boundary fixups

Tests assert the properties, not the timings. Sharded output equals sequential across a fixture exercising every layer, plus shard boundaries and edge shapes. ## Summary
`entire disable --uninstall` reported success while leaving an external agent's hooks installed.

Reproduced on a repo with `external_agents: true` and an external plugin whose `are-hooks-installed` reports true:

```
$ entire disable --uninstall --force

Uninstalling Entire CLI...
  Removed Claude Code hooks
  Removed git hooks (5)
  Removed .entire directory

Entire CLI uninstalled successfully.

$ # subcommands the plugin was asked to run: (empty — it was never executed, not even `info`)
```

The plugin's hooks stayed on disk, and because `.entire/` (settings included) had just been deleted, what remained was a set of agent hooks calling into an Entire that is no longer installed there.

## Cause
`runUninstall` reaches agents only through the registry, and nothing on that path ever ran external-agent discovery, so an external agent was not in the registry to be uninstalled: absent from the confirmation summary, its `UninstallHooks` never ran, and its hooks survived an uninstall that reported success.

## Fix
`external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways(ctx)` at the top of `runUninstall` — **ungated, deliberately**. The `external_agents` setting that gates discovery lives in `.entire/`, which this very command deletes. After a partial uninstall (plugin hooks left behind, `.entire/` gone) a gated re-run could never see the plugin again, making the uninstall unrepeatable. Ungated discovery keeps every removal step isolated from the others, at the accepted cost of executing `entire-agent-*` binaries on `$PATH` even in repos that never enabled them.

On top of that:

- **One hooks-installed sweep per uninstall.** The confirmation summary and the removal share the same `getAgentHookState` result — for an external agent each probe is a subprocess, and reusing it means the uninstall removes exactly what the user was shown.
- **Uninstall acts on the sweep's answer, for built-ins and plugins alike.** An agent that cleanly reported no hooks is left alone — `uninstall-hooks` is a mutating call, and discovery registers every `entire-agent-*` on `$PATH`, not just the one the user enabled.
- **`AreHooksInstalled` now returns `(bool, error)` across the agent interface.** Every agent had been collapsing "I cannot tell" (unreadable config, malformed JSON, a plugin that crashed or timed out) into "no hooks installed". An agent that could not answer lands in an `unchecked` set: named in the confirmation summary on its own line, warned about with its own error, and **not** asked to mutate state it never claimed to own.
- **`entire agent remove <name>` fails on a broken check** instead of uninstalling blind — that path targets one agent the user named, so they can fix the config and re-run.
- **The recovery command is one a plugin will accept, and one Windows can run.** It carries `cd <repo-root>`, `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`, and `ENTIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` (the protocol promises all three), quotes paths with spaces, and prints a PowerShell shape on Windows. `TestPluginUninstallCommand_PerOS` pins both shapes.
- **Usable without a terminal.** The confirmation prompt now has an `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` guard pointing at `--force` instead of a bubbletea internal error (which also made the test suite hang under a pty).

## Exit-code contract: any failed step fails the command
There is **no `--strict` flag** (it existed mid-branch and was dropped). The uninstall has a single contract: any step that fails — built-in agent hooks, external plugin hooks, git hooks, session states, `.entire/`, shadow branches — exits non-zero and closes with `Uninstall did not complete — see the warnings above.` A run never reports a success it could not verify:

- An external plugin whose `uninstall-hooks` fails is named with both remedies: re-run `entire disable --uninstall` (discovery is ungated, so a re-run reaches the plugin again), and the direct `entire-agent-<name> uninstall-hooks` command, since the plugin binary itself may be what is broken.
- An **unchecked** agent (probe crashed, errored, or printed junk) also fails the run. Its hooks "may still be installed" — an unknown state is not a clean "none". Unchecked externals get the same two remedies; unchecked built-ins are reported with the read/parse reason (removal would read the same broken file, so it is not attempted, and no plugin command applies).
- The `"Entire is not installed in this repository"` early return requires every agent to have been *checked*: any unchecked agent falls through to the removal phase, so a repo whose only leftover is an unprobeable plugin no longer silently claims "not installed" on re-run.
- The only exception is the user's own Ctrl-C: a cancelled context is reported as an interruption ("run again to finish"), not charged to the agent it happened to kill — still non-zero, but no per-agent blame or recovery command.

Known tradeoff, on purpose: because discovery is ungated and an unanswerable plugin fails the run, a broken `entire-agent-*` binary anywhere on `$PATH` fails `entire disable --uninstall` in every repo until it is fixed or removed. A wrong "uninstalled successfully" was judged worse than a loud failure with a printed remedy.

## Problem

Commit-to-session linking guesses by worktree path: the commit hooks match `SessionState.WorktreePath` against the commit's worktree. Any drift between bookkeeping and reality loses the linkage. This has bitten three times — during the work behind PR #1647, PR #1287, and PR #1991 (the PRs themselves are unrelated; the linkage loss struck the sessions building them): an agent committing in a sibling worktree gets an unlinked commit — or, with a poisoned state dir, a **wrong** link. The latest instance: `agentimport` tests missing repo isolation leaked fixture sessions (`sessC` et al.) into the developer's real `.git/entire-sessions`; prepare-commit-msg linked a commit to the `sessC` fixture and stamped a trailer whose checkpoint was never written — a dangling trailer, repaired only by manual session-state surgery.

## Change

**Identity-first linking.** An agent-made commit is attributed by *who made it*, not *where it happened*:

- Identity is the owner fingerprint the codebase already records: `SessionState.Owner`, the `proclive.Identity` that `captureSessionOwner` persists on every turn start (proclive walks past shells, the `entire` binary, and the Go toolchain to the long-lived agent — so a human commit typed in the same terminal never matches; Cursor bugbot's high-severity finding on the first cut, plus the trail review's duplication finding, both land here). No new recording, no new state field, no new platform code: the earlier `internal/proctree` package was reviewed as a duplicate of `proclive` and deleted. New `proclive.CurrentAncestry()` snapshots the hook's ancestor chain once — one hostname read, one boot-id read, one proc walk — and `Ancestry.Depth` matches every candidate in memory with proclive's host, boot, and start-time guards, so a recycled PID or an identity from another machine can never match and the per-commit cost no longer scales with the number of session states; `HasAncestor` remains as the single-identity convenience over it. On platforms proclive cannot introspect (Windows), identity matching reports nothing and linking falls back to worktree matching — honestly, rather than via untested platform code.
- Commit hooks match each session owner against the snapshot — was this process spawned, however indirectly, by that session’s agent? When owners at different depths both match (a nested agent and the outer agent that spawned it), the **nearest ancestor wins** — the process closest to the commit is its author; interaction recency only breaks ties within one depth (the same agent hosting several sessions, e.g. after a resume). The match is **unioned** with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement — a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree, and identity adds the one path matching missed.
- **Guest-linking:** Any session matched outside its home worktree is guest-linked, whether identity-matched or selected by the pre-existing single-worktree fallback. It condenses the transcript and records trailer state while touching nothing else: no BaseCommit advance, shadow-branch deletion, or carry-forward from the foreign worktree. This also fixes the legacy fallback path, which previously could orphan the home shadow branch.

Net effect: **an agent commit links to its session in any worktree, automatically** — no `session adopt`, no retro-attach. `adopt` shrinks to its migration role.

**Hardened worktree fallback** (human commits, severed process trees):
- Imported sessions never link (historical records; a leaked imported fixture is exactly what hijacked the sessC commit).
- Multi-worktree ambiguity filters to sessions that interacted within 15 minutes: one recent worktree links; two recent worktrees still decline. This intentionally turns some cases the old code refused into a best-candidate link; recentSessionWindow is a correctness tradeoff because a session in a long-running build or tool call can age out and leave the other worktree to win. The decline is announced on stderr with the remedy (entire session adopt), but only from the commit-linking path and only when identity matching could not rescue the commit either; amend and post-rewrite stay silent.
- Identity failure is diagnosable: unresolvable ancestry (restricted `/proc`, sandbox denials) and all-shell chains log at Debug at both record and match time, so "identity never works on this host" is visible in a doctor bundle instead of being masked by the fallback forever.

**Leak closed at both ends:**
- `agentimport` scopes its session-state writes to the repo being imported into (new `session.NewStateStoreForWorktree`, which rejects empty roots) instead of the process CWD — a production bug, not just a test bug.
- Under `go test`, both store constructors refuse to open outside the temp root, so any future non-isolated test **fails loudly** instead of writing fixtures into a real repo. The full unit suite (8,973) passes with the guard on — the agentimport tests were the only leakers in the repo.

- Four-agent toolkit review (`f561bab64`): guest condensation previously still ran the shadow-delete/remaining-files/carry-forward paths with cross-worktree data (critical, fixed); the adopt hint printed before identity rescue, false-positively, twice per commit, and on amend/rebase (critical, fixed); plus negative-path diagnostics, pure `isSessionHomeWorktree`, TurnStart ancestry refresh, store-guard coverage for the explicit-root constructor, single state listing per hook, halved proctree call counts, `tmux: server`/empty-exe classification, tombstone exclusion, and comment/doc drift.

- `mise run fmt` clean, `mise run lint` 0 issues, full unit suite 8,973 pass, integration suite 480 pass, Vogon canary green.

## Which skill names are sent

Skill names are arbitrary user tokens, so the emitted `skill` property comes
from a closed vocabulary: a recognized Entire skill name, or one of two fixed
categories (`custom`, `entire:unlisted`). Recognition matches the leaf name
after stripping Entire's plugin namespace — not the `entire:` prefix itself,
which comes from whatever plugin the user installed or authored and so vouches
for nothing.

Two scoping choices, both taking the direction whose error is visible:

- **Unlisted Entire skills still count.** The leaf list lives in this repo
  while the skills ship from `entireio/skills`, so a skill released upstream
  before the list is updated reports as `entire:unlisted` — a lagging list
  undercounts the per-skill breakdown but never adoption volume.
- **Unnamespaced installs are not matched.** Entire's skills are advertised as
  cross-agent and can arrive without a namespace (Pi normalizes
  `/skill:<name>` to a bare name; a hand-copied `SKILL.md` has none), and
  those report as `custom`. Matching bare leaves would fold Claude Code's
  built-in `/review` and any local `/search` into Entire's numbers — an
  overcount invisible in the data, where this undercount has a known cause.
  Worth revisiting if cross-agent installs become a meaningful share.

`entireio/pr-review-toolkit` skills are deliberately out of scope: the CLI's
install hints for it are still placeholders (`skilldiscovery/registry.go`), so
nothing ships under that namespace yet.

**Which paths actually emit.** The condense path (commit and session-end) is
where transcript-extracted events reach telemetry in practice. The turn-end
snapshot around `HandleTurnEnd` only yields events when the turn had mid-turn
commits — `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` early-returns on an empty

Raw search-command counts can't say whether adoption is low — most sessions have nothing worth searching for. | Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `used_search` | Did the session invoke `entire search`? **Omitted** when not measurable — see below. |

The event is named for the **commit**, not the checkpoint, because every property is commit-scoped: `files_committed` counts that commit's files, and `prior_ai_history` asks whether commits *before* this one touched them — which is what the probe's `--skip=1` is for. Implements #2058's durable pointer model for subagent work, with the subtree payload location (`tasks/` inside the parent session's checkpoint).

## The incident

A real session dispatched ~29 background Claude Code subagents; entire captured nothing beyond a 2–8s launch stub for each one, even though the agents ran 5–18 minutes. The root cause: Claude Code's PostToolUse for a backgrounded Task tool fires at the **launch acknowledgment**, before the subagent has done any work — the real completion is delivered later, out of band, as `SubagentStop`. Entire never registered a hook for that true-completion signal, so every background subagent's edits and transcript were invisible.

## Verified hook facts

- **`SubagentStop`** fires per-agent at true completion, including after the parent's own turn already ended. Payload carries `session_id` (parent), `agent_id`, `agent_transcript_path` (the subagent's own transcript), `tool_use_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`. Notification-only; default timeout 600s.
- Subagents fire **no session-lifecycle hooks of their own** (no SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionEnd) — `SubagentStop` is the only completion signal, and a finishing subagent does not fire the parent's `Stop`.
- Subagent transcripts live at `<project>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl`; the launch-time PostToolUse payload's `tool_response.agentId` matches that filename (verified against 29 real transcripts).

Parsing stays defensive: an absent `agent_transcript_path` degrades to the agent-layout convention (`ResolveAgentTranscriptPath`) rather than failing, and the parser logs the raw payload's key names (never values) at Debug.

## Design: durable task records + condensation materializer

**Task records** (`session.TaskRecord`, json `task_records`, on session state) are the durable ledger: `ToolUseID`, `AgentID`, `StartedAt`, `SubagentType`, `TaskDescription`, `DeclaredTranscriptPath`, `Files`, `TokenUsage`, `CompletedAt` (zero = live/in-flight). Mid-turn a record is a **pointer, not a payload** — the subagent transcript stays where the agent wrote it, and the record remembers how to find it. Producers:

- **Background launch** creates a live record (labels captured at launch because `SubagentStop`'s payload carries none of them).
- **Foreground tasks** create-on-completion.
- **SubagentStop / foreground post-task / SessionEnd sweep** complete exactly-once via `strategy.CompleteTaskRecord` — one `MutateSessionState` closure: claim `CompletedAt`, attach files/tokens/declared path, merge into the session's `FilesTouched`. Completion happens last, after successful extraction, so a failed capture leaves the record live for the SessionEnd sweep to retry; a racing duplicate completes nothing.
- **Factory Droid Workers** upsert (`UpsertCompletedTaskRecord`): multi-turn workers merge files into one record instead of claiming exactly-once.

**Materializer**: condensation resolves each record's transcript (declared path first, agent-layout fallback), runs the same sanitize → externalize → redact pipeline as the session transcript (`prepareTaskTranscriptForStorage`), and writes `tasks/<toolUseID>/{agent-<agentID>.jsonl, task.json}` **inside the parent session's checkpoint** on `entire/checkpoints/v1` — both backends, via the shared `applySessionWrite`. An unresolvable/unreadable/empty transcript still gets a `task.json` with a stable, path-free unavailable reason. Poisoned records (empty/unsafe IDs) are skipped-with-warn, never allowed to wedge condensation.

**Self-contained checkpoints**: live records store transcript-so-far on every condensation and survive for retry; completed records are removed only after a successful write (`removeCompletedTaskRecords` off `resetCheckpointWindow`). A mid-task commit carries a partial transcript; a later checkpoint carries the full one.

**Trigger currency**: `State.HasTaskContent()` (`len(TaskRecords) > 0`) replaces the deleted `TranscriptOnlyTaskSteps` counter everywhere. Records-only sessions (no shadow branch, no steps, empty parent transcript) condense; records never live on the shadow tree, so shadow-branch existence no longer implies task content (shadow pinning keys on `StepCount` only).

## Alignment with #2058

This PR implements #2058's core — a durable record that survives until condensation, plus a materializer that makes every checkpoint self-contained — choosing the **subtree payload option** (`tasks/` inside the session checkpoint) over a separate task checkpoint kind. There is now exactly **one producer path** into stored task data (the materializer); the never-reachable per-write `IsTask` persistent route and its `Entire-Metadata-Task` trailer (#2058's "dead writer") are deleted.

## What was removed and why

Once every checkpoint is self-contained, the mid-turn backstops are redundant — they existed only because task data used to die if it wasn't snapshotted before the session ended:

- The turn-end incremental snapshot backstop (rotation, growth-dedup, cap of 8), `persistCapturedTranscriptSize`, `IncrementalTypeBackgroundProgress` / `FormatBackgroundProgressSubject` / `FormatIncrementalSubject`.
- The per-write `IsTask` persistent route + `Entire-Metadata-Task` trailer (dead code, see above).
- `claimTaskRecord`-as-removal: completion now marks, never deletes — the materializer needs the record.
- `SaveTaskStep` is now formally incremental-only (errors on `!IsIncremental`); its sole production caller is the Claude Code post-todo hook.

## Behavioral invariants preserved

- Background launches stay lazy: no capture at the launch stub, only a record.
- Foreground completion still merges the subagent's files into the session's `FilesTouched`.
- Exactly-once completion (the old claim-and-remove dedup, reshaped as mark-completed-once).
- SessionEnd ordering: the live-record sweep runs strictly before `endSessionNow`'s eager condense, so that condense materializes it.
- Read-only subagents' transcripts are stored: a completed record with no files still materializes, and "has records" makes the session condensable.
- The late-arrival zombie guard: a `SubagentStop` for a missing session state skips outright; `PhaseEnded` state → complete + eager condense.

## Deliberate behavior changes

- (a) Turn-end no longer writes incremental background snapshots — in-flight visibility now comes from condensation materializing the transcript-so-far into each checkpoint.
- (b) `doctor --force` **condenses** record-bearing dead-owner sessions instead of discarding them.
- (c) Shadow branches are deletable while records exist — records don't live there.
- (d) Record-bearing sessions are PrepareCommitMsg trailer candidates via `sessionHasNewContent`.
- (e) `checkpoint list --pending --json` task rows carry empty `id`/`metadata_dir` (no shadow commit exists); external consumers keying on `id` should use `tool_use_id`. Rows render with accurate `Running`/`Completed` verbs.
- (f) `SaveTaskStep` errors on non-incremental use.

## Repairs shipped alongside

- Hard-killed agents' live records get a terminal state: `finalizeExitedSessions` (the `entire status`/`doctor` sweep) completes live records before ending the session, so their transcript-so-far reaches a permanent checkpoint.
- `CondenseSessionByID` materializes instead of clearing when records exist; orphan cleanup can't `Clear` record-bearing states.
- ENDED + `FullyCondensed` is terminal-healthy even with leftover live records — pre-fix states self-resolve, no migration.

## On-disk compatibility

Old state files' `transcript_only_task_steps`, `last_captured_transcript_bytes`, and `last_snapshot_attempt` keys are silently dropped on the next save; no migration. Nothing durable shipped under the old `in_flight_tasks` schema.

## OPF / redaction

**git-branch (the default primary): task transcripts get the full 9 layers, automatically.** The pre-push OPF rewrite walks the checkpoint tree subtree-recursively and treats every blob except `content_hash.txt` as redactable, so `tasks/<id>/agent-<id>.jsonl` and `task.json` are covered with no new wiring. This PR writes no `content_hash.txt` into the task directory, so the apply pass's sibling-`full.jsonl` hash recompute is undisturbed.

**git-refs: OPF now runs there too — fixed in this PR.** It previously ran on *nothing* on that backend: `prePush` returns for refs before ever reaching the OPF block, and `RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF`'s only call site was the git-branch path, so session transcripts and task transcripts alike shipped at 8 layers while a user who enabled OPF believed 9 ran. That gap was pre-existing and backend-wide — not a consequence of the subtree design and not specific to tasks — but this PR enlarges it by volume (subagent transcripts are the highest-volume, least-reviewed content in the system), so it is fixed here rather than deferred.

`RewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF` (`strategy/manual_commit_opf_refs.go`) mirrors the v1 rewrite and reuses its machinery rather than duplicating it — the same blob walk and open blob policy, the same raw-byte and leaf-byte caps, the same single batched OPF shell-out per push, the same error taxonomy, and the same two up-front fail-closed gates in the same order. Only discovery and update differ, and both are simpler on refs: the push queue already names exactly which refs are unpushed, so there is no merge-base or divergence analysis, and each ref is updated independently instead of CAS-ing one branch tip.

Every unpushed commit on a queued ref is rewritten, not just its tip — pushing a ref sends its whole unpushed ancestry, so a tip-only rewrite would have shipped un-redacted ancestor blobs alongside the redacted tip. The walk stops at the first commit already carrying `Entire-OPF-Applied`, which makes the trailer its own watermark: in steady state it stops at the tip's parent and costs nothing. A repo that enables OPF late is bounded by the existing `resolveBootstrapLimit` / `BootstrapTooLargeError` pair rather than rewriting unbounded history.

**Failure semantics differ by backend, deliberately.** Both fail closed. git-branch aborts the user's `git push`. On refs, unflushed refs simply stay queued, so an OPF failure or an explicit abort withholds the flush and returns cleanly: nothing un-redacted ships and the user's push still succeeds. It is not silent — a `logging.Warn` plus a stderr line say that checkpoint refs stayed queued and why. `OPFSkip` (the user opting out for one push) is unchanged: flush as-is, 8 layers, no trailer.

One user-visible copy change on the previously-untouched v1 path: `BootstrapTooLargeError` now says "N checkpoint commits" instead of naming `entire/checkpoints/v1`, because the error is shared across both backends and a git-refs user has no v1 branch. The remediation is identical for both.

- **Shadow-only capture (#2058) — FIXED on this branch**: subagent transcripts no longer die at the user's commit; the materializer writes them into every permanent checkpoint under `tasks/`, on both backends.

Because eligibility is keyed off a no-TTY commit plus a fresh task record, the trust window spans the entire lifetime of a background task — including raw-mode TUI git clients (lazygit, gitui, tig) that spawn `git commit` without a real terminal. We accept this: a mislink is recoverable (and rare — it requires a fresh record plus an unrelated no-TTY commit in the same narrow window), while a silent unlink is not. TITLE: fix(strategy): prevent duplicate session-end checkpoints
Fixes #2035.

Session-end condensation could make a checkpoint durable before its updated session state was saved. If the hook was killed in that window, recovery still considered the transcript unfinished and could write it again under a different checkpoint ID.

On current `main`, the immediate `PostCommit` path described in the issue no longer reproduces this for a no-files session because that path discards it. The durable failure still reproduces through `entire doctor`, which sees the ended session as unfinished and previously generated a new checkpoint ID for the same transcript range.

### Approach

This PR uses a write-ahead checkpoint ID. It saves the intended ID as `CondensationAttemptID`, writes the checkpoint with that ID, advances the session bookkeeping, and then clears the pending attempt. If the process dies after the write, the next attempt reuses the same ID instead of creating a duplicate.

The reservation is also honored during commit preparation and `PostCommit`. If `PostCommit` receives a different checkpoint ID, it preserves the interrupted session and shadow branch rather than overwriting its recovery state.

Advancing `LastCheckpointID` or `CheckpointTranscriptStart` before writing would prevent duplication but introduce a data-loss window: state could claim that a transcript was saved when the checkpoint write had failed. The pending ID records durable intent without claiming that the write succeeded.

`CondensationRecoveryPending` separately records when recovery may need to reconcile an interrupted write created by an older CLI version. This keeps the more expensive storage lookup out of normal condensation paths.

Reserved writes are routed using their checkpoint ID format. If checkpoint configuration changes between reservation and retry, the checkpoint is still written to the backend that originally generated its ID.

### Recovering state from older CLI versions

Older interrupted sessions have no pending checkpoint ID. Doctor reconciles them using the session identity, transcript bounds and content, checkpoint counts, agent and turn metadata, touched files, and session kind. Externalized images are reinserted before comparing transcripts.

Storage listing or reading failures stop recovery and preserve its state for another retry rather than being treated as “checkpoint not found.” If the session has genuinely advanced, recovery creates a new checkpoint instead of reusing the older one.

### Related findings

`checkpoint list` exposes both duplicates because they have different checkpoint IDs, while `tokens profile` can count both and inflate checkpoint-observed token totals. The latter already warns about overlapping checkpoint history.

Codex kills timed-out hook process groups with `SIGKILL`, not `SIGTERM`, so Entire cannot print its normal termination message during a Codex timeout. See Codex’s [hook runner](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/bb701f1e8c8db884fa0cdafff4b8dcb1604f2fdd/codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs) and [process-group cleanup](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/bb701f1e8c8db884fa0cdafff4b8dcb1604f2fdd/codex-rs/utils/pty/src/process_group.rs).

### Follow-up plan

This PR lands the non-destructive part first: it prevents new duplicate checkpoints, makes retries deterministic, and reconciles interrupted writes from older CLI versions. It deliberately does not remove or hide duplicate pairs that already exist.

Questions for a follow-up:

1. Should existing duplicate pairs remain as physical history and be collapsed only in `checkpoint list` and `tokens profile`, or should `doctor` repair the stored history?
2. If one checkpoint becomes canonical, which should win: the original session-end write or the later recovery write? What should happen when their metadata differs?
3. Should repair be automatic, an explicit doctor action, or reporting-only until the user chooses?
4. Should transcript-range idempotency become a shared rule for every condensation entry point, or remain limited to session-end and doctor recovery?

Once those product choices are clear, existing duplicates can be handled separately without coupling destructive cleanup or changed read semantics to this durability fix.

### Verification

Regression coverage includes pending ID reuse, legacy orphan reconciliation, repeated storage read failures, recovery-marker persistence, mismatched commit IDs, backend changes between reservation and retry, and advanced sessions receiving a genuinely new checkpoint.

## The design (after merging #2032's durable-record model)

1. **Trigger (idle + task content).** `tryAgentCommitFastPath` now treats a session as eligible when it's ACTIVE **or** IDLE with a fresh task record (`idleWithTaskContent`, `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`). A record counts whether it's still in flight or completed-but-unmaterialized — the same `HasTaskContent()` shapes condensation keys on — and each record is bounded by its own `StartedAt` against `activeSessionInteractionThreshold` (24h), so a subagent that dies without ever sending `SubagentStop`/`SessionEnd` doesn't leave the session a trailer candidate forever. The same predicate feeds `shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck`'s overlap-check bypass, so the trigger and the condensation trust share one rule.
2. **Content (the condensation materializer).** The base branch (#2032, issue #2058) made `session.TaskRecord` a durable ledger: condensation materializes each record's transcript-so-far into the checkpoint's `tasks/<tool-use-id>/{agent-<agent-id>.jsonl, task.json}` subtree, live records survive for the next condensation, and every checkpoint is self-contained. That means the trailer this PR adds is backed by content *by construction*: the very condensation the trailer triggers stores the subagent's transcript-so-far. The earlier revision of this PR pre-wrote a commit-time transcript snapshot (`captureInFlightTaskCommitSnapshot` / `captureInFlightTasksForCommit`) gated on `headHasCheckpointTrailer` to keep the trailer from dangling — all of that is now removed as redundant, along with its tests and post-commit wiring.

## Overlap-trust scoping

`idleWithTaskContent` is deliberately scoped to `PhaseIdle` only, not `PhaseEnded`. An earlier version leaked the overlap-check bypass to ended sessions too; that shape was empirically reproduced and fixed (`fe2aa5fdb`), with a regression test pinning that an ended session with a lingering record still declines — its records belong to its own final condensation, not this fast path.

## The trade-off

Because eligibility is keyed off a no-TTY commit plus a fresh task record, the trust window spans the entire lifetime of a background task — including raw-mode TUI git clients (lazygit, gitui, tig) that spawn `git commit` without a real terminal. This means an unrelated no-TTY commit made while a background task happens to still be running could get mislinked. We accept this: a mislink is recoverable (and rare — it requires a fresh record plus an unrelated no-TTY commit in the same narrow window), while a silent unlink is not. Records are genuine evidence of live agent work, not a guess. The window is also narrower than it used to be: the base branch's dead-owner sweep completes a crashed agent's records, so orphaned records no longer linger for the full 24h in the common case.

## Non-regression pins

- An ordinary commit made while IDLE with **no** task records stays exactly as before: no trailer (`TestSubagentCheckpoints_IdleCommitNoMarkers_NoTrailer`).
- Record-less behavior (foreground tasks, ACTIVE-session commits) is byte-identical to pre-PR behavior — the new eligibility branch is additive.
- The end-to-end arbiter, `TestSubagentCheckpoints_CommitWhileIdleWithLiveMarker_LinksAndCondensesContent`, drives the real prepare-commit-msg + post-commit hook chain and now asserts the strong guarantee: the mid-task commit's condensed checkpoint **contains `tasks/<id>/agent-<id>.jsonl` with the subagent's real transcript content** (stronger than the previous revision, which could only check the pre-written shadow-side snapshot).

1. ~~**Pre-existing orphan-prune gap.**~~ **Fixed by #2032.** `findSessionsForWorktree`'s orphan sweep now spares record-bearing sessions (`!state.HasTaskContent()` in the prune predicate), so an idle session whose only activity is one open task record survives to `prepare-commit-msg` — a first-turn background commit links. 2. ~~**Sweep-finalize follow-up.**~~ **Fixed by #2032.** `finalizeExitedSessions` now completes a dead-owner session's live records (`sweepCompleteLiveTaskRecords`, `session_finalize.go`) before ending it, exactly as a clean SessionEnd does — preserving transcripts and closing the trust-window trade-off from the other end.

Claiming a commit is bounded separately: only a record within `idleWithTaskContent`'s 24h window may mint a trailer. Two reviewers reproduced it end to end; `staleRecordIsOnlyContent` closes it, and PostCommit now warns whenever a trailer is minted and no session condenses into it, so any future divergence is visible rather than silent.

An earlier revision of this PR also exempted record-bearing sessions from PostCommit's read-only skip. That is reverted: the skip only fires when another session's files are in the commit, and PostCommit hands one checkpoint ID to every condensing session, so that other session fills the trailer anyway. The exemption prevented no dangling trailer and only let a record-bearing session condense into someone else's commit.
